The construction described indeed gives a set of 338 350 triples that hits every infinite sequence, but it is far from optimal. The known theory of unavoidable word sets shows that much smaller hitting sets exist; for example, a minimal unavoidable set of length 3 over an alphabet of size m has size on the order of m² (precisely m² − m + 1 in many cases). For m = 100 this gives a bound around 9 900, not 338 350. Therefore the claimed minimum n = 338 350 is not correct.

VERDICT: REJECT (the final answer is not correct)
